ai.description: *Cyrtodactylus tripuraensis* reaches 70 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark transverse bands and a distinct precloacal groove. It lacks precloacal pores and possesses enlarged femoral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus tripuraensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark nuchal loop and a series of 6–8 dark, irregular transverse dorsal bands.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus tripuraensis* inhabits the moist deciduous forests of Tripura, India, typically found on tree trunks and rock surfaces at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Tripura Bent-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively forage for small insects and invertebrates along rocky surfaces and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus tripuraensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from May to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus tripuraensis* is endemic to the state of Tripura in Northeast India, where it is found in hilly forest habitats at elevations between 200 and 600 meters.
